title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 11: Ang Bagong Bayani v. Comelec — Party-List
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
keywords: Ang Bagong Bayani-OFW Labor Party v. Comelec
primary_topics: Chapter 11: CJP on Ang Bagong Bayani-OFW Labor Party v. Comelec, determining who qualifies under the party-list system and how winners and nominees are counted
sub_topics: Veterans Federation Party v. Comelec — four parameters (20% allocation, 2% threshold, three-seat cap, proportional)
Ang Bagong Bayani — party-list must represent the marginalized and underrepresented
Guidelines for qualifying party-list groups and their nominees

cases: Ang Bagong Bayani-OFW Labor Party v. Comelec

stances.claim: The party-list system is reserved for the marginalized and underrepresented; major parties and the unqualified may not exploit it.

notable_anecdotes: Veterans Federation Party (October 6, 2000) first set the four party-list parameters.
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 11 analyzes Ang Bagong Bayani-OFW Labor Party v. Comelec, which — building on Veterans Federation Party v. Comelec and its four parameters (the 20% allocation, 2% threshold, three-seat cap, and proportional distribution) — held that the party-list system is reserved for the marginalized and underrepresented, and set guidelines for qualifying groups, winners, and nominees under RA 7941.
